disabled.reason: fapi.binance.com (USD-M) and dapi.binance.com (COIN-M) both returned HTTP 451 on 2026-09-27 with the venue's jurisdiction-restriction message. Unlike Binance spot, these hosts have no market-data-only mirror, so no fixture could be captured. Binance is one of the largest derivative venues, so its absence materially reduces Atlas's funding and open-interest coverage; this is stated in docs/LIMITATIONS.md rather than hidden.

Reachable on 2026-09-27, but the instrument catalogue returned from the network used to build this release was not representative of the venue: /api/v1/instrument/active returned 12 unlisted placeholder spot pairs with listing dates in the year 2200, /api/v1/instrument/activeIntervals returned empty arrays, and XBTUSD (the venue's flagship perpetual) was reported with state "Settled". An adapter cannot be validated against a catalogue that does not reflect the venue's real state. Re-capture from an unrestricted network before enabling.

Every Bybit API host (api.bybit.com, api.bytick.com, api.bybit.nl) returned HTTP 403 from a CloudFront edge with the body "The Amazon CloudFront distribution is configured to block access from your country" on 2026-09-27. No live payload could be captured, so no fixture exists and no parser could be written against a verified schema. Writing one from memory would violate the project's rule against inventing response fields. The adapter is a documented stub. To enable it, capture fixtures from an unrestricted network and follow the adapter checklist in CONTRIBUTING.md.
